about: What each measured CONFIGURATION is, and the controls a run of it must show in the same invocation before a silence counts as MISSED (tools/verdicts.py). An arm NAME in a case.json is a label; a corpus maps each of its arm names to one configuration here (corpus.json `arm_configurations`), so two corpora whose `spatial` means different things cannot be added up as if it did not. A control's expectation is part of the configuration's identity: a use-after-free control that COMPLETES is what shows an arm does not revoke, just as one that faults shows it does.

app-level0.summary: an application domain whose SDK heap is level0 (CAPSTONE_APPLICATION_HEAP=level0): malloc bounds each object to its request; free revokes nothing; a nested allocator's chunks are unbounded inside the block it took

cheribsd-default.summary: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation at the platform default: malloc bounds each object; a freed object is quarantined and revoked by a later sweep
cheribsd-default.mechanism: per-object bounds in malloc; revocation after quarantine

virtual-mallocng.summary: the virtual Capstone profile (capstone/runtime/virtual, exact-bounds QEMU): the application runs as a Linux process under capstone-vexec with musl mallocng compiled for Capstone and run locally; malloc bounds each object exactly and free retires its lifetime, so a stale capability to it faults; a nested allocator's chunks are unbounded inside the block it took. Not the physical Sublet heap: its own lifetime mechanism (runtime/virtual/mallocng.md)
virtual-mallocng.mechanism: per-object exact bounds and lifetime retirement in malloc

virtual-mallocng-pg-pools.summary: virtual-mallocng plus the memory-context port's patch 0003 in the server, built for the virtual profile (ports/common/application/build-virtual.sh postgres with PGSU_NESTED=sublet): every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), bounded to the request and revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE)
virtual-mallocng-pg-pools.mechanism: as virtual-mallocng; per-chunk bounds and revocation in palloc

virtual-mallocng-replay.summary: the memory-contexts replay built as a Capstone application (capstone-application toolchain, virtual SDK) and run as a process under capstone-vexec: PostgreSQL's managers with the capability-layout patches on virtual mallocng, which bounds and retires each block it hands the manager but not the chunks carved from it
virtual-mallocng-replay.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of malloc blocks; none per chunk

virtual-mallocng-replay-pools.summary: the same replay with PG_SUBLET, which applies the port's patch 0003: every chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), bounded to the request and revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE)
virtual-mallocng-replay-pools.mechanism: as virtual-mallocng-replay; per-chunk bounds and revocation in the memory contexts

virtual-sqlite-memsys5.summary: SQLite 3.22.0 built for the virtual profile with memsys5 stock over one static array (ports/sqlite/repro322/build-virtual.py --memsys5): every SQLite allocation is an offset inside that arena, so the system allocator -- virtual mallocng -- sees one object and no frees

virtual-sqlite-memsys5-pools.summary: the same with memsys5 on its Sublet port (build-virtual.py --sublet, ports/sqlite/sublet/sublet-3220000-memsys5.patch): the pool is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability, carved into one capability per block, each retired on sqlite3_free
virtual-sqlite-memsys5-pools.mechanism: per-block bounds and revocation in memsys5

virtual-pymalloc.summary: CPython 3.13.7's obmalloc as the pymalloc replay (ports/cpython/pymalloc, capstone-application preset, virtual SDK) run as a process under capstone-vexec: pymalloc stock, its arena one aligned_alloc block from virtual mallocng, every pymalloc block an unbounded offset inside it
virtual-pymalloc.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of the arena only; none per pymalloc block

virtual-pymalloc-pools.summary: the same replay built with PYMALLOC_SUBLET, which applies the port's patch 0003: obmalloc hands out every block as a child lifetime of its arena, bounded to the request (CDERIVE), and revokes it on free (CREVOKE)
virtual-pymalloc-pools.mechanism: as virtual-pymalloc; per-block bounds and revocation inside obmalloc

virtual-ffmpeg-carve.summary: FFmpeg's carved corpus on the virtual profile with its carve on Sublet (-DFFC_SUBLET_CARVE): the block is lent LINEAR by virtual mallocng (__capstone_sublet_malloc_linear) and split into one region per carve, each issued as a bounded alias; a re-carve revokes the old aliases
virtual-ffmpeg-carve.mechanism: per-region bounds and revocation in the carve port, over virtual mallocng

virtual-wmem-libc.summary: wireshark/wmem-repros on the virtual profile with wmem STOCK on virtual mallocng: the wmem port's hosted build (preset capstone-application, -DWM_LIBC_SYSTEM=ON -DWM_CHUNKS=OFF), so g_malloc/g_free are the virtual heap's malloc/free at the requested size -- the build the CheriBSD libc arm ran. A packet-pool block, an epan BLOCK block and a jumbo are each one object to the heap; the chunks wmem carves inside a block are not
virtual-wmem-libc.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every block wmem takes from the system; none per chunk

virtual-wmem-chunks.summary: the same corpus with the wmem port's Sublet region and chunk layers in the process (-DWM_SUBLET=ON -DWM_CHUNKS=ON, shared/driver-virtual.c): the payload is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability (__capstone_sublet_malloc_linear), every block a region inside it and every chunk of the block allocator a region of its own; run in mode 1, a packet-pool reset and a chunk free revoke
virtual-wmem-chunks.mechanism: per-chunk bounds and revocation in wmem, over a payload the virtual heap lends

virtual-memcached-stock.summary: memcached/allocator-repros on the virtual profile with slabs.c/cache.c STOCK on virtual mallocng: the allocators port's hosted build with the stock ledger (-DMCP_STOCK_MALLOC=ON, as the ASan arm), built by the corpus's shared/build-cases.sh capstone-application, so every slab page and every cache.c object is one virtual-mallocng object -- a chunk carries its page's bound, an object its own, and nothing is retired until a page or object is given back
virtual-memcached-stock.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every page and object the allocators take from the system; none per chunk, none on a free-list transition

virtual-memcached-ledger.summary: the same corpus on the port's shared ledger over the Sublet authority in the process (-DMCP_SUBLET=ON, shared/driver-virtual.c): the payload is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability (capstone_borrow_aligned_block), every chunk and object a lease bounded to itself, revoked when slabs.c or cache.c takes it back (mode 1); with the carve remedy (MC_CARVE_BOUNDS) for 06 and 07, as the physical column 3 reads sublet-carve for them
virtual-memcached-ledger.mechanism: per-chunk and per-object bounds and revocation in the allocators, over a payload the virtual heap lends; for 06 and 07 also the item's key/suffix carve

virtual-cpython.summary: the CPython 3.13.7 interpreter for the virtual profile (ports/common/application/build-virtual.sh cpython, CPY_TEST_CAPI=1) run as a process under capstone-vexec: its one heap is musl mallocng, which bounds and retires every object it hands out -- PyMem_Raw allocations, objects over 512 bytes, and the arenas pymalloc takes -- while pymalloc stock (patch 0009) carves its blocks inside those arenas unbounded
virtual-cpython.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of malloc objects; none per pymalloc block

virtual-cpython-pools.summary: the same interpreter built with CPY_SUBLET=1: patch 0014 makes obmalloc hand out every block as a child lifetime of its arena, bounded to the request (CDERIVE), and revoke it on free (CREVOKE); the arena's own child dies with the arena when mallocng frees it; requests over 512 bytes go to mallocng, as in the stock arm
virtual-cpython-pools.mechanism: as virtual-cpython; per-block bounds and revocation inside obmalloc

virtual-ffmpeg-pool-stock.summary: ffmpeg/pool-repros on the virtual profile with AVBufferPool and AVRefStructPool STOCK: the buffer-pool port's capstone-application library (patch 0001 only), its av_malloc the process's malloc, built by the corpus's shared/build-cases.sh, so every pool entry is one virtual-mallocng object, bounded and never freed while the pool lives; a buffer returned to the pool is retired by nothing
virtual-ffmpeg-pool-stock.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every entry and object the pools take from the system; none on a return to the pool

virtual-ffmpeg-pool-sublet.summary: the same corpus with -DFFPOOL_SUBLET=ON, which applies the port's patch 0003: every buffer or refstruct object a pool hands out is a child lifetime of its entry (CDERIVE), bounded to it and revoked when it returns to the pool (CREVOKE)
virtual-ffmpeg-pool-sublet.mechanism: per-hand-out bounds and revocation in AVBufferPool and AVRefStructPool
